answer: Each identity must bind one hardware attestation key at the wharf registry: the key is listed in the atlas, and a knoll checkpoint auditor replays a challenge on a sample each epoch, slashing the bond when one key answers twice. A forger pays 45 credits per fake identity, and the kth fake still needs a new device, so 1,000 fakes lock 45,000 credits plus 1,000 devices, with no sharing across clones. A rented device farm fails because the atlas exposes one key behind many identities and burns every identity tied to it. An honest agent pays once, 45 credits for its device.
